tasks.short: Keep technical knowledge current through reading, seminars and practical evaluation.

steps.what: Review recurring incidents and identify knowledge gaps.
Find relevant manuals, technical articles and upcoming seminars.
Read selected material and work through technical examples.
Attend seminars and question presenters about practical problems.
Judge which techniques suit the supported environment.
Write and share useful learning with the support team.

loop.input: Selected notes, source references and the specialist's applicability decisions.
loop.output: A short learning brief with source references and proposed support improvements.
loop.check: Require a source for each technical claim; the specialist checks accuracy before sharing.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; missing evidence returns the brief to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies headings but cannot condense varied prose into a useful explanation.

tasks.design: Configure topic subscriptions and saved searches in {DOCS}, informed by recurring incidents in {HELPDESK}. A bounded drafting loop turns selected notes into a cited learning brief for review before sharing through {CHAT}; reading, questioning and practical evaluation remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources are scattered, and deciding what deserves attention requires knowledge of the supported environment. Collecting material was easier to automate than learning from it.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured subscriptions handle collection, while a small drafting loop reduces the effort of sharing lessons. AI-assisted coding can help connect incident categories to source filters, without assuming a particular speed gain.
tasks.still_hard: Deep understanding, useful questions and testing whether advice fits local configurations still take time. Source subscriptions may require licences.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognises misleading advice, connects new knowledge to past incidents and learns through practice.

ambition.what: Monthly troubleshooting clinic for reception staff.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into finding material and writing summaries; more goes into practice and teaching. The specialist can choose clinic topics within an agreed remit, with no added production-change authority.

reach.task: Resolve common workstation and meeting-room problems before escalating.
reach.learn: Observe reception workflows and learn how to teach short, accessible troubleshooting routines.

evidence.claim: Configured source filters and incident reports can reduce collection work; learning itself still requires practice.
TOPdesk drafts knowledge items for human review, supporting the feasibility of reviewed knowledge drafting.

assumptions: Shares are illustrative estimates for a learning cycle, not measured customer time.
Approved technical sources provide searchable content or subscriptions.
Build ranges cover a small source collection and one support team.
Collection is automated only within selected topics; the specialist still chooses what to study.
No employee-level learning or productivity scoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which source subscriptions and content licences are available?
Are incident categories reliable enough to inform learning priorities?
Can the specialist reserve time for practice and a reception clinic?
What access and consultation are required for the proposed data use?
research_questions: How accurately do topic filters identify useful material for the supported hardware and software versions?
new_work: Maintain source lists and topic filters.
Check draft briefs against original sources.
Remove obsolete guidance and handle conflicting advice.
Keep incident examples free of unnecessary personal data.

tasks.short: Assess office automation options through workflow observation, space assessment and cost comparison.

steps.what: Agree the study question, constraints and success criteria.
Observe staff performing the workflow and discuss exceptions.
Survey equipment locations, space constraints and accessibility needs.
Collect workload, delay and incident figures from available records.
Compare implementation costs, running costs and benefit scenarios.
Write feasible options with dependencies, risks and space implications.

loop.input: Observed workflow, measured constraints, calculated costs and specialist-selected options.
loop.output: An options paper separating evidence, assumptions, dependencies and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Link factual claims to supplied records; copy financial results from calculated fields; specialist reviews feasibility.
loop.stop: One draft and two targeted revisions; unsupported claims remain marked unknown and return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but describing trade-offs across varied observations requires prose synthesis.

steps.what: Validate options with affected staff and the process owner.
Approve the study recommendation or request further evidence.

tasks.design: A reusable study generator on {DATA_PLATFORM} imports approved records from {HELPDESK} and {PROJECT}, then calculates cost scenarios from explicit assumptions. A bounded loop drafts an options paper in {DOCS}; staff validate operational effects and the operations manager approves the recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Studies are infrequent and differ in scope. Baselines, quotes and observations arrive in different formats, making a reusable process costly to assemble.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable import mappings, calculation templates and document generation reduce repeated assembly work. A bounded loop can organise free-text observations without choosing the investment.
tasks.still_hard: Observed time savings may not become cash savings. Physical constraints, accessibility, organisational resistance and incomplete workload records require fieldwork and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist notices workarounds, challenges optimistic assumptions and explains trade-offs to affected people.

ambition.what: A fixed-scope feasibility review for small reception and administrative teams.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling tables and more time observing work and testing assumptions. They can recommend a pilot within an agreed study remit; investment approval remains with the budget holder.

reach.task: Assess a proposed change to appointment handling or document processing.
reach.learn: Learn workload sampling, capacity planning and the difference between released time and cash savings.

evidence.claim: Explicit cost formulas, scenario tables and templated reports can automate study assembly without automating investment judgement.
A field study reported more completed developer tasks with coding assistance; this does not establish feasibility-study savings.
GDPR applies to identifiable workflow observations; employee consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed monitoring.

assumptions: Shares describe a small study that includes both workflow and space assessment.
Build ranges cover reusable tooling for a limited set of record formats, not the fieldwork for every study.
The initial baseline uses aggregate workload figures rather than individual productivity scores.
Consent and access effort includes consultation under national rules where required; elapsed approval time may be longer.
The study decision does not authorise purchasing or production deployment.
unknowns: Which workload records exist and what do their timestamps mean?
Are supplier quotes and internal cost rates available?
Who owns the process and approves the recommendation?
What consultation is required for observation or changes to working methods?
Which floor plans and accessibility constraints are current?
research_questions: Which sampling method gives a useful baseline without collecting unnecessary employee-level data?
new_work: Maintain import mappings and cost assumptions.
Check draft claims against observations and calculations.
Investigate missing or inconsistent baseline records.
Compare pilot outcomes with the original benefit assumptions.
Refresh access, retention and consultation arrangements when study scope changes.

tasks.short: Select and supervise staff delivering technical projects, troubleshooting and installations.

steps.what: Agree project scope, required skills and staffing needs.
Prepare the role brief and staffing request.
Review candidate evidence against agreed role requirements.
Interview candidates and assess technical and collaborative skills.
Approve the appointment recommendation and employment terms.
Assign project work, responsibilities and escalation paths.
Coach workers, resolve blockers and direct technical problem-solving.
Check progress, dependencies and unresolved installation issues.
Accept completed work against agreed technical criteria.

tasks.design: Configure role templates and approval routing around {ATS}, and reusable assignment checklists and progress views in {PROJECT}. Link project issues to {HELPDESK} and acceptance evidence in {DOCS}; people select candidates, coach workers, approve assignments and accept completed work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision mixes relationships, staffing judgement and administration, so it was treated as one indivisible activity. Progress evidence is often split between project records and incident records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates, task dependencies and dashboard configuration can remove repeated coordination work. Small deterministic connectors can join records without introducing automated employee assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Fair hiring, conflict resolution, coaching and judging readiness remain personal responsibilities. Reliable status data requires workers to record meaningful progress.
tasks.human_edge: The lead recognises developing capability, handles disagreement and balances delivery pressure with safe, sustainable work.

ambition.what: Offer supervised technical project placements to customer service staff.

tasks.altitude: The lead spends less time assembling updates and more time coaching and unblocking work. Within an agreed project remit, they can allocate bounded learning assignments; hiring and production-change rights do not expand automatically.

reach.task: Allocate work and coach staff during a service-process change.
reach.learn: Learn structured coaching, workload balancing and how to assess learning assignments fairly.

reach.task: Triage simple technical enquiries during a supervised placement.
reach.learn: Learn safe diagnostic scripts, escalation limits and clear incident recording.

evidence.claim: Configured task templates, dependencies and progress views can reduce administrative coordination while supervision stays human.
Recruitment and worker-management AI can fall within EU AI Act Annex III; this design excludes automated candidate ranking and worker scoring.
GDPR and applicable national employment and consultation rules affect candidate data and employee monitoring.

assumptions: This supplemental task is performed by a senior specialist with delegated team-lead duties.
Shares represent a combined staffing and project-supervision cycle; hiring is intermittent.
The recruiter handles offer issue and onboarding through the wider hiring workflow.
Assignment suggestions use approved task templates and availability, without inferring employee performance.
Build ranges cover one team and existing recruitment and project processes.
Consultation effort is conditional on national rules and changes to employee monitoring; elapsed approval time may be longer.
unknowns: What hiring, assignment and acceptance authority does the specialist hold?
How often does this role participate in recruitment?
Are availability and project status records current?
Can project and incident records be linked with appropriate access?
What employee consultation is required for new progress views?
research_questions: Which team-level progress indicators reveal delivery blockers without becoming individual productivity scores?
new_work: Maintain role templates, assignment checklists and escalation paths.
Review proposed assignments before they reach workers.
Correct stale availability and progress records.
Review access to candidate and employee information.
Check that dashboards remain focused on work dependencies rather than worker rankings.

tasks.short: Adapt commercial software through supported configuration and small extensions.

steps.what: Clarify the requested behaviour and agree acceptance criteria.
Check documented configuration options, extension interfaces and support restrictions.
Configure the {OTHER} commercial application in a test environment.
Write necessary extensions in the {OTHER} development environment.

loop.input: Approved requirements, supported interfaces, relevant existing code and test fixtures.
loop.output: A small extension patch and proposed tests in an isolated development workspace.
loop.check: Run syntax, security and regression checks; specialist reviews the diff and interface compatibility.
loop.stop: At most two patch attempts per bounded change; failing checks or unsupported interfaces return work to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use configuration first. Where it cannot express the required behaviour, writing a new extension requires contextual code synthesis.

steps.what: Run regression checks using {OTHER} software testing tools.
Validate changed behaviour against real work examples.
Release accepted changes through the {OTHER} application administration console.
Update the change record and configuration history.

tasks.design: Use supported configuration in the {OTHER} commercial application before building extensions. For genuine gaps, a bounded coding loop drafts a patch in the {OTHER} development environment; deterministic checks produce evidence in {HELPDESK}, users accept behaviour, and the application owner approves release. Generate change records in {DOCS} from the release manifest.
tasks.previous_blocker: Small changes still require environment knowledge, testing and release coordination. Unsupported customisations create upgrade risk, while manual configuration is difficult to reproduce.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable configuration templates, test fixtures and release manifests reduce repeated work. Coding assistance can draft bounded extensions, but its benefit depends on the application and the specialist's review effort.
tasks.still_hard: Undocumented interfaces, weak test coverage, licensing restrictions and upgrades can make extensions expensive. Passing automated checks does not prove that a change fits real work.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides whether a request merits customisation, recognises unsupported approaches and negotiates acceptable behaviour with users.

ambition.what: A supported configuration clinic for small customer service teams.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time repeating configuration and change paperwork, and more time shaping requirements and reviewing behaviour. They can select approved configuration patterns within a defined remit; release authority remains with the application owner.

reach.task: Describe repetitive case-handling steps and validate a proposed configuration change.
reach.learn: Learn service workflows, acceptance-example writing and how configuration affects frontline handling.

reach.task: Improve reusable response templates and document-routing rules.
reach.learn: Learn document controls, exception routing and accessible template design.

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot supports code completion and review with expected human oversight, supporting bounded patch drafting.
Developer field trials reported increased completed tasks with coding assistance; this does not establish a tenfold build-speed gain.
A controlled study found experienced developers slower with early assistance tools, showing that review and context costs can outweigh gains.
Supported configuration, reproducible tests and controlled releases are feasible without autonomous production access.

assumptions: Shares describe a mixed workload of configuration changes and small extensions; configuration-only requests skip extension work.
The target application exposes supported configuration or extension interfaces.
Build ranges cover a reusable path for one application and one small pilot change.
The coding loop has isolated development access and no production credentials.
Test data is synthetic or minimised under GDPR.
National consultation requirements are assessed if changes affect working methods or employee monitoring; elapsed approval time may exceed the effort range.
unknowns: Which application and supported extension mechanisms are involved?
Are test environments, rollback facilities and representative fixtures available?
Who owns acceptance and release decisions?
What do support terms and licences permit?
Which personal data would development and testing expose?
What access and employee consultation are required?
research_questions: Which requested behaviours can be met through supported configuration before any extension is considered?
Which regression checks detect the application's most consequential failure modes?
new_work: Review generated patches and configuration differences.
Maintain regression fixtures and supported configuration patterns.
Handle failed checks and unsupported requests.
Maintain release permissions, rollback procedures and generated change records.

role.altitude: The role shifts from collecting information and maintaining coordination records toward technical judgement, user coaching and controlled service improvement. Additional decision rights should be explicit: selecting learning topics, proposing bounded pilots and choosing approved configuration patterns within an agreed remit.
reach: Help receptionists resolve common workstation and meeting-room problems.
Help administrative supervisors assess workflow changes and benefit assumptions.
Coach customer service staff through supervised technical triage placements.
Help correspondence clerks improve response templates and routing rules.
skills_to_grow: Deterministic testing, release evidence and rollback.
Coaching, fair selection and workload allocation.
GDPR data minimisation and consultation under national rules.
role.ambitious_version: Become a technical service improvement lead who runs small feasibility reviews, teaches frontline troubleshooting and delivers supported configuration changes with clear evidence. People retain hiring, investment and release decisions; reusable tools make preparation and follow-through cheaper.
